“The Waltz Of The Little Girls” -- Also played in D

I’ve always lliked this tune. I think it works better on the fiddle in D.
Here is ABC courtesy of Fiddler’s Companion. This is pretty much the way I play it:
X:1
T:Waltz of the Little Girls, The
D:The Pearl, Phil Cunningham/Aly Bain
C:Trad/Rasmussen
N:Originally in Eb
Z:Nigel Gatherer
M:3/4
L:1/8
K:D
dc BA|F2 FE DE|F2 dc BA|F2 FE DF|G2 GF GA|B2 BA GF|E2 EF GA|
B2 BA Bc|BAdc BA|F2 FE DE|F2 dc BA|F2 FE DF|G2 GF GA|B2 BA GF|
E2 EF GA|Bd/B/ Ac Ac|d2::DF Ad|c2 cB AF|DF BF AF|E3 A Ec|
d2 DF Ad|c2 cB AF|DF BF AF|E3 A Ec|d2:|]

It’s credited to a Terry Rasmussen but I do not know who that is. I learned it from Grey Larsen circa 1982, he’d just picked it up in Europe. He was touring a lot then, and a lot of people in the US got it from him around that same time.

“La Valse Pour Les Petites Jeunes Filles” / “The Waltz Of The Little Girls”

In the past these alternate takes were only found in the ‘Comments’. Then, years back, our webmaster Jeremy made changes in the software where anything of ABCs moved up, including partials, and with bits going missing. Not all standards with ABC notation were recognized. Hopefully now I’ve sorted out those missing bits here, at least for my transcriptions, and they should make considerably more sense now.

If problems remain, please let me know and I’ll do my best to make it right. This sort of problem happened throughout the site and when I catch them, or someone lets me know, I do the corrections. We, the collective ‘we’, myself and others, were sometimes a bit haphazard in entering ABCs in the Comments, and that included partials, incomplete transcriptions and fragments. In that great ‘transformation’ those gnarly bits also tended to move up…

Keep safe, keep sane, keep active - ‘c’

The Waltz Of The Little Girls, X:9

Trying to make sense of the structure of this tune, I see the other submissions have the first four notes inside the repeat of the A section whereas it seems more like a pickup measure to me, so I put it outside. But having done that the first measure of the B part, which doesn’t seem like a pick up measure, now starts before the repeat.

↳ Posted by Mike Floorstand on October 18th, 2023.

Re: The Waltz Of The Little Girls

It’s fairly standard practice to put the pickup inside the repeat, especially if it helps avoid or shorten second time endings. Some people though prefer full bars.

Re: The Waltz Of The Little Girls

I recently emailed Grey Larsen to ask him about the origin of this tune, and here’s what he wrote back:

"I learned it in 1978 from a Belgian fiddler named Raymond Honay when he was traveling in the US. I don’t know if there is a known composer. I think it is probably a traditional French or Belgian tune.

Malcolm Dalglish and I recorded it on our 1982 album, Thunderhead. I think this may have been the first recording of the tune. I played in on a Hardanger fiddle, in F (the instrument was tuned a minor third higher than a regular fiddle, thus the tune came out in F). Raymond played the tune in D.

It was in Cincinnati, Ohio that I met Raymond and learned the tune from him (among others). He was traveling with his friend and button accordionist André Fonsny. They stayed with Malcolm and I for a number of days in Cincinnati, and the next year we visited them in Belgium. We learned many tunes from them including some bourées that we also recorded on the Thunderhead album."
